reviews.note: Feet together at 82% is a clear narrow-base fault and the only issue, so widening the stance is the right lead.
90% is a genuine 10-point miss with everything else clean, so a quick cue to widen the base is fair to lead with.
145% is clearly too wide and it shows in the slow recovery, so trimming the base is the correct primary fix.
138% is solidly over the line and the only fault, so narrowing the base is the right call.
75% with feet under the hips is a clear narrow stance and the sole issue, so widen the base first.
178 degrees is essentially straight legs with no power base, so loading the legs is exactly the right lead.
172 degrees is two degrees over ideal with an otherwise clean swing — too marginal to make the headline note.
132 degrees is a genuinely deep load that hurts recovery, so easing the squat is the right primary cue.
138 degrees is only two degrees deep and nearly in range — not worth flagging as the number-one fix.
175 degrees with little leg drive is a real upright-load fault and the only issue, so lead with loading the legs.
128 degrees is a clearly deep squat that will slow recovery, so softening the bend is the correct lead.
12 degrees of separation on an arms-only swing is a clear kinetic-chain breakdown — exactly the right thing to lead with.
18 degrees is barely two under the minimum on an otherwise solid swing — too borderline to headline.
8 degrees is almost no hip-shoulder separation, a major power leak, so the kinetic chain is the right primary fix.
15 degrees is meaningfully under ideal and limits the chain, so leading with hip turn is correct.
19 degrees is one degree shy of ideal — that is measurement noise, not the headline fix for this swing.
A paddle stopping at the waist at -0.25 is a clearly truncated drive finish, so completing the follow-through is the right lead.
-0.05 is a hair below shoulder and effectively a complete finish — too marginal to make the top recommendation.
-0.4 is a badly short finish that kills drive depth, so extending the follow-through is the correct primary fix.
-0.15 is a real low finish with the rest clean, so leading with a fuller follow-through is fair.
-0.3 below shoulder is a clearly incomplete drive finish and the only fault, so lead with the follow-through.
88% is a genuine narrow-base fault and a reasonable lead, though the upright knee is also worth a mention next.
It led with the upright knee, but the low hip turn here is the higher-leverage kinetic-chain fix I would lead with.
With both a low hip turn and short finish present, leading with the 12-degree kinetic-chain breakdown is the right priority.
It led with a wide stance, but the incomplete follow-through is the more important late-phase fix to lead with.
-0.1 is only a touch low on an otherwise good swing — too borderline to be the number-one note.
95% is just under ideal and well within normal variation — not worth headlining for a player swinging well.
171 degrees is one degree over ideal — that is noise, not the primary fix to lead with.
17 degrees is only three under the minimum and the rest is clean — too marginal to make the headline.
132% is two points over the line — a borderline wide base I would not lead with as the top fix.
